title: Shiv — Discover
description: Private discovery feed: stimulating new episodes from follows + new shows. Curated for Apple Podcasts.
author: Shivanshu Chaudhary

items.title: 687. Are Prediction Markets the Best Forecasting Tool Ever — or Just Another Casino?
items.description:
Idea: when markets price beliefs, they expose whether institutions want truth-seeking forecasts or just sports-bet liquidity dressed as civic tech.
Sharpens taste: watch how Kalshi/experts frame ‘information’ vs entertainment — the same power move behind every dashboard you trust.

items.title: The loan at the heart of a new foreclosure crisis
items.description:
DSCR loans let rental cash-flow underwrite the borrower — a quiet financial redesign that scales portfolios until one Baltimore stack shows how ‘innovation’ re-imports GFC risk.
Systems craft: watch the underwriting rule, not the marketing label.

items.title: The Domino’s Pizza Tracker Theory of Everything
items.description: Economics-not-founder gem: the Domino’s tracker as labor illusion — progress UI that makes waiting feel like work being done. Institutional craft hiding in a pizza app.

items.title: Talent, Time and Money: The Curse of General Magic
items.description:
It's 1990. A new company called General Magic is going to build its vision of the future: the smart phone. They have talent, almost unlimited cash, and a 15 year head start on the iPhone. What could go wrong? Based on David Epstein's book Inside the Box: How Constraints Make Us Better.

General Magic had talent, unlimited cash, and a 15-year head start on the iPhone — and still lost.
Idea: constraints as competitive advantage, not romantic scarcity. Harford/Epstein turn a Silicon Valley cautionary into a decision-design lesson.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/talent-time-and-money-the-curse-of-general-magic/id1484511465?i=1000788891693

items.title: Annie Lowrey on the Time Tax, Fraud, and Rationing by Paperwork
items.description:
Annie Lowrey's new book, The Time Tax, argues that the most regressive levy in American life is the hours each of us must spend on hold, in waiting rooms, and filling out forms a competent state would have pre-filled — roughly fifty a year on average, and far more if you're poor. Tyler spends much of this conversation pressing the opposite case, asking whether that bureaucracy is quietly serving a useful purpose by rationing knee surgeries that don't work, deterring fraud, or screening for immigration.

Why this sharpens your taste: Tyler’s steelman (bureaucracy as rationing/fraud filter) vs Lowrey’s “time is the regressive tax” — learn to argue policy as design, not vibes. Craft move: treat inconvenience as a deliberate lever, then ask who it actually screens.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/annie-lowrey-on-the-time-tax-fraud-and-rationing/id983795625?i=1000790017400

items.title: Incentives Are for Losers (with Adam Mastroianni)
items.description:
Incentives matter, sure. But what should you do when following the incentives means quietly participating in something wrong? Psychologist Adam Mastroianni argues that obeying bad incentives--shading a headline for clicks, keeping the found wallet because no one's watching--is "loser behavior," a surrender of the hardest and most human task: figuring out right from wrong for yourself. In this wide-ranging EconTalk conversation, he and Russ Roberts explore Le Guin's "Omelas," the "big fish" you glimpse that could upend your whole life, and Charles Sumner's near-fatal courage. They wrestle with whether good incentives or good people matter more, why lavish academic salaries may attract exactly the wrong scholars, and the moral lessons of marriage.

Why this sharpens your taste: "loser behavior" flips the incentives-as-excuse — when the scoreboard rewards the wrong thing, the hard skill is refusing the scoreboard.
Omelas/Sumner pairing: moral clarity as operator discipline, not vibes.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/incentives-are-for-losers-with-adam-mastroianni/id135066958?i=1000789541014

items.title: Show 74 - Mania for Subjugation IV
items.description:
The stage is set for an in-person showdown between Alexander and Persia's Great King. The resulting Battle of Issus, although often ignored by Hollywood, is one of the most important battles in all ancient history. It gets its due here.

why this sharpens your taste:
1) Carlin’s craft: long-arc narrative that treats conquest as incentive design and systems failure — not battlefield trivia.
2) Builds patience for power dynamics across centuries; the antidote to news-cycle history.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/mania-for-subjugation-iv/id173001861?i=1000779313976
